translations.answer: Cannot rely solely on UI. The project maintainer explicitly states that GPU simulation/Fabric will suppress USD read/write, so runtime properties and transform do not appear in the UI; observation of the UI can be achieved with the debug flag --device cpu env.sim.use_fabric=false. However, there is no closed-loop effect on whether threads influence runtime performance: subsequent replies indicate that custom gains will take effect, but the original author claims that he has already used the same ImplicitActuatorCfg but it still does not work. Therefore, the visibility of the UI and runtime gain should be validated separately, and neither can be used as the final fix.
translations.applicability: Applies to diagnosis of ImplicitActuatorCfg and Fabric/USD UI in Isaac Sim 5.1/Isaac Lab GPU simulation. Actual gain must be measured independently on the target commit and assets.
translations.credibility.rationale: The answer has not been closed or there is a conflict in the sources; the conclusion is not fully resolved.
translations.details.attempts.0: The maintainer suggests running with --device cpu env.sim.use_fabric=false to observe runtime changes in the UI.
translations.details.attempts.1: Subsequent replies indicate that custom gains will take effect, but the original author claims that he has already used the same ImplicitActuatorCfg but it still does not work.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Separate UI/USD visibility from PhysX/Fabric runtime values: it is a known behavior that GPU Fabric does not display UI changes.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: When checking USD side debug values, use CPU and disable Fabric; whether runtime is effective should be evaluated with controlled dynamic response or lower-level buffer comparison.
translations.details.environments.0: Isaac Lab, Isaac Sim 5.1, Python 3.11, Ubuntu 24.04.3, RTX 5080, driver 580.95.05; manager-based PPO template, UR-with-gripper USD; original post did not provide Isaac Lab commit.
translations.details.limits.0: CPU + disable Fabric is a recommended display/debug setting; original author did not report execution results, so it cannot be considered as a resolved actuator gain.
translations.details.limits.1: Threads do not read PhysX runtime buffer, step response, joint trajectory, or independent torque comparison; changes in UI and penalty cannot be used to determine actual gain.
translations.details.limits.2: Issue was closed, but the final technical reply still indicates that the same configuration did not work, and the closed state cannot be used as evidence for a closed-loop system.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The thread only explained the mechanism behind UI not reflecting changes in GPU/Fabric mode; it did not prove that the gripper stiffness/damping were in effect during runtime, nor was it associated with any PR or final fix.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: When the ImplicitActuatorCfg stiffness/damping are not displayed in the Isaac Sim UI, are the parameters truly ineffective, and how can we distinguish between a UI display issue and a runtime issue?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Before migrating a policy or controller to real hardware, it should be verified through small, controlled responses to identify equivalent stiffness/damping, and limits on torque, velocity, and position should be imposed; direct calibration based on UI single values is not acceptable.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The UI not updating was explained by the maintainer as a result of GPU simulation being used to speed up USD read/write operations.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: Actual stiffness/damping settings are not effective in a closed-loop system: the responder claims they will be effective, but the original author, using the same configuration, still states they do not work.
translations.details.symptoms.0: After setting finger_joint stiffness=280, damping=28, the Isaac Sim UI still displays the original value from the USD file.
translations.details.symptoms.1: The original author suspects the parameters were not applied, as the joint-velocity penalty significantly increased.
translations.details.symptoms.2: Despite obtaining the same ImplicitActuatorCfg example, the original author still claims the configuration does not work.
translations.source.locator: Isaac Lab #4320 comment 3707421315 explains GPU/Fabric UI behavior; comment 3725503782 claims gain is effective; comment 3914083197 states the same configuration still does not work.
translations.source.title: In Isaac Lab GPU/Fabric, actuator gains not appearing in the UI must not be conflated with whether they take effect at runtime
